title: Synchronizing Collaborative Inventory Dashboards
business: Logistics companies managing real-time warehouse stock levels across multiple regional distribution centers.
problem: Users experience data staleness when multiple warehouse managers update stock counts simultaneously, leading to inconsistent UI states where one manager sees outdated inventory levels while another has already committed a change.
solution: TanStack Query manages server state by providing a unified caching layer that automatically synchronizes remote data with the UI. By utilizing query keys, the library tracks specific data sets, allowing for background refetching and manual cache invalidation to ensure the UI reflects the most recent server-side state after a mutation.
steps: Define a unique query key for inventory items to enable granular cache tracking.
Implement useQuery to fetch initial stock levels, allowing the library to handle background caching and deduplication.
Execute stock updates using the useMutation hook to modify server-side data.
Trigger queryClient.invalidateQueries within the mutation's onSuccess callback to force a refetch of the stale inventory data.
Configure staleTime and gcTime to balance between cache freshness and memory management.
outcome: Managers see consistent, up-to-date inventory counts across all active sessions without manual page refreshes or complex state synchronization logic.
limitation: The primary limitation is the potential for excessive network requests if cache invalidation is triggered too aggressively. Developers must monitor the frequency of refetches to ensure they do not overwhelm the API, which can be checked by observing the network tab in browser developer tools to verify that invalidation only occurs when necessary.

By using manual state management to store every stock change in a global variable.
By utilizing query keys to track data and invalidating the cache to force a background refetch.
By disabling caching entirely to ensure every request hits the server directly.
